plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies a 28.27 × 22.68 mm left atrial myxoma adherent to the posterior wall; the in-text description specifies a pedunculated mass.
Caption explicitly states that the mass is attached to the fossa ovalis.
Patient tumor histology, identified by the caption as cardiac myxoma, shows scattered stellate/spindle cells in abundant pale myxoid stroma.
Gross photograph of the patient's surgically removed left atrial myxoma shows a small rounded, lobulated, reddish-brown polypoid mass.

in_text_mentions: TTE showed a 28.27 × 22.68 mm pedunculated mass in the left atrium, adherent to the posterior wall (Fig. 1A)and accompanied by mild mitral regurgitation (MR). There was no evidence of ventricular inflow obstruction. Laboratory values and electrocardiogram(ECG) results were normal. We convened a multidisciplinary team composed of obstetrician, cardiologist, surgeon and anesthetist to discuss the management. Since a fetus of this gestational age could survive after birth with a low risk of premature complications and surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during pregnancy may carry a risk of

A 32-year-old gravida 5, para 2 woman was referred to our hospital at 17 weeks’ gestation with symptoms of palpitations and shortness of breath. TTE showed a mobile, pedunculated 19 × 10 mm mass in the left atrium (Fig. 1B) attached to the fossa ovalis. No mitral regurgitation was revealed. The cardiac rhythm was regular and no murmurs were heard in any of the valve regions of the heart. Her lungs were clear. No symptoms of peripheral embolization were found. The blood tests did not show any positive results. ECG revealed an incomplete right bundle-branch block.

After cardiovascular, surgical and obstetrical consultations, surgical excision was recommended. At 18 weeks’ gestation, the patient experienced a removal of the tumor via totally endoscopic minimally invasive cardiac surgery. CPB was continued for 46 min, and the duration of aortic cross clamp was 21 min. Normothermia was applied to the patient during CPB. A 20 × 15 mm mass was eliminated from the left atrium. Pathological examination indicated a myxoma(Fig. 1C). TTE suggested that there were no residual mass, either during or after the operation.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real echocardiographic patient image showing a mobile right-atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum, a specific intracardiac manifestation compatible with the disease-focused article. Right-atrial location is a recognized less common presentation, so it is classified as a variant. [raw subtype: right atrial cardiac myxoma] B: Real color Doppler echocardiographic patient image showing the same mobile septally attached right-atrial mass. It is compatible with a cardiac myxoma manifestation in the disease-focused article; the right-atrial location is a recognized less common variant. [raw subtype: right atrial cardiac myxoma]

Upon review of the echocardiographic findings of the 8 patients described in our study, it is essential to highlight the fact that a thrombus can mimic a myxoma and thereby create a diagnostic conundrum. In the case of atypical echocardiographic features of an atrial mass, a thrombus should be considered. If a mass can be dissolved with anticoagulants, then it is likely a thrombus; other
